attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his Substack post, written in his own voice.

semantics.note: This is a present-perfect observation. In context, 'other approaches' means alternatives to LLM scaling, especially in the US. The drafter's 'AI approaches other than LLMs' is slightly broader but acceptable.

contract.note: The plain reading (alternatives got a small share relative to LLMs) is fair and ordinary. Using 2023 as a proxy period is a contractor choice the speaker did not supply. The flags correctly note that the result depends on what counts as 'other approaches' and 'investment'.

evidence.note: Covers global private AI investment in 2023, with generative AI over a quarter. Non-generative AI is not the same as non-LLM research toward trustworthy AI, so this neither supports nor contradicts the claim.
Funding record for one DARPA neuro-symbolic program, about $10–14M. It shows that alternative research exists, but a single program gives no aggregate share.

reviews.rationale: No dataset in the packet compares investment in LLMs with investment in alternative technical approaches under a consistent classification. The Stanford split uses a different category and covers the whole world. The DARPA item is a single program. The evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his post.

semantics.note: 'Profits will be elusive' is firm 'will' language, so it is a scored forecast. 'Given the cost of chips' is kept as an asserted cause. No horizon was stated.

contract.note: Reading this as sustained difficulty earning net profit across LLM developers is a fair plain reading. The speaker gave no accounting basis or duration, and the early-resolution rule sensibly requires a sustained, representative outcome.

evidence.note: The Anthropic S-1 shows a GAAP net loss for H1 2026, driven mainly by fair-value changes on financing instruments. It also shows a small operating loss and positive adjusted operating income. That is one company over one interim period, and chip costs are not isolated as the cause.

reviews.rationale: This is an open-ended forecast with no deadline. The single interim filing shows mixed signals across profit measures and does not attribute losses to chip costs. The early-resolution rule's sustained, representative outcome is not established, so the claim is not scored yet.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion. The surrounding quotes from Andreessen and Efrati are separate from it.

semantics.note: This is a present-perfect observation. Adding 'from scaling' is faithful to the surrounding context, which discusses scaling running out.

contract.note: Reading diminishing returns as smaller capability gains per proportional increase in scale is fair and ordinary. Choosing 2024 up to the publication date as the window is reasonable.

evidence.note: An observational scaling-law study finding that performance is predictable. It does not measure whether returns at the frontier declined in 2024.

Reuters reports Sutskever saying pretraining results have plateaued, and anonymous sources describing delays. This is consistent with the claim but is expert opinion without resource-normalised measurements.

reviews.rationale: No item gives a comparable, resource-normalised series showing smaller capability gains per unit of scaling during 2024. The Reuters report is suggestive but anecdotal, and the arXiv study does not address the question. Unresolved.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: This is a compound claim. Calling scaling-to-AGI 'just a fantasy' is a firm, open-ended negative forecast. The valuation part is a causal claim about the present. The drafter kept both parts and the scaling qualifier.

contract.note: Splitting the technical forecast from the valuation attribution is fair. Requiring independently validated AGI from scaling alone to contradict the forecast matches the speaker's words.

evidence.note: OpenAI's own disclosure that pretraining scaling continued. This bears on the antecedent, not the outcome, and does not show that AGI was produced. Treated as context, not support.
OpenAI's own disclosure of benchmark results for a model combining several approaches. It is not independent validation of AGI and does not isolate scaling.
OpenAI's $157B valuation in October 2024. It gives no breakdown of how much of that value comes from AGI expectations.
Microsoft describes established product lines. This does not measure what share of its valuation rests on AGI expectations.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no independently validated AGI from scaling and no impossibility result, so the open-ended forecast is not resolved. It also has no credible breakdown of either company's valuation. All items are company disclosures or context. Unresolved.
